requirements.text: Introduction letter. Tell us who you are and who will sign the contract for your firm. Keep it to one page.
About your firm. How big is it, where are its offices, how long has it advised public employers, and how many public employers does it advise now?
Your people. Who will be chief negotiator? Who will back that person up? Who will handle day-to-day advice and hearings? Give each person's background and attach resumes at the end.

Bargaining record. List the public sector negotiations your proposed chief negotiator has led in the last six years. For each one, name the employer and the union, and say how long bargaining took and whether it went to impasse.
How you would run our negotiations. Describe how you would prepare, how you would work with our bargaining team, how you would keep the Board informed, and what you would do if bargaining stalls.
Hearings and advice. Describe your experience in grievance arbitration and labor board proceedings, and how you handle a steady flow of small advice questions without running up fees.
References. Give us four public employer references. At least two must be able to speak about your chief negotiator at the bargaining table.

Conflicts. Have you or anyone at your firm ever represented the Wexcombe Library Workers Guild, Service Employees Local 4410, or any employee of the Library District? Tell us about that and about any other possible conflict.

Price. Give hourly rates for every person named in #3. Offer a fixed monthly fee for day-to-day advice if you are willing to. Tell us what you would charge for travel and what expenses you would bill.
Taking over. Our current counsel is retiring. How would you get up to speed on our contracts, open grievances and bargaining history before March?

extra_fields.source_line / source_line_no: on each deadline: the line of the RFP file (stripped, 1-based number) that states the date in force. For a date changed by addendum it is the addendum line; original_source_line is the line in the body.
extra_fields.section, numbered, text: on each requirement: the section it sits in, whether the RFP gives it a number or label, and its exact text with runs of white space collapsed to one space (the label itself is left out).
extra_fields.alt_labels, alt_qtypes: other labels or question types that a scorer should also accept. Question types are the test author's judgement.
extra_fields.deleted_requirements: requirements removed by addendum. They must NOT appear in the parsed requirement list.
extra_fields.evaluation_as_issued, forms_as_issued, b: values before any addendum, for checking that the change is shown.
extra_fields.addendum (on addendum_changes): which addendum made the change. Kinds beyond the existing keys: requirement_deleted, criterion_removed, weight_changed, insurance_changed, form_removed; time_from and time_to are given where an addendum changes the time of day.
extra_fields.amount_value: insurance amount as a whole number of dollars.
extra_fields.dates_that_are_not_deadlines: dates in the text that must not be read as schedule deadlines.
extra_fields.not_requirements: numbered or lettered items that are not proposal requirements (scope of services, general conditions, table of contents). Reading them as requirements is an error.
extra_fields.kind_not_in_existing_keys: marks a deadline kind the existing keys do not use; score it separately.
